context._comment_mounts: The image carries its own bnxt_re provider; the host provider directory is mounted as well so ibverbs resolves it either way.

docker_build_arg.RDMA_CORE_VERSION: <FILL_RDMA_CORE  empty to keep the base image rdma-core; 63.0 is the Broadcom-Thor2 bnxt_re EFAULT fix, see references/cluster-types.md>
docker_build_arg.RCCL_CMAKE_OPTIONS: <FILL_RCCL_CMAKE_OPTIONS  extra cmake -D flags, e.g. -DFAULT_INJECTION=OFF; empty for RCCL defaults>

slurm._comment_skip_gpus: This cluster's SLURM rejects the generated --gpus-per-node directive; without this the job is refused before launch.
slurm._comment: On Broadcom-Thor2 add "skip_gpus_directive": true - that cluster's SLURM rejects the generated --gpus-per-node directive. Do NOT set it on a cluster that allocates GPUs through GRES: the job would then be submitted with no GPU request at all.

distributed._comment: One container per node owning all 8 GPUs. nproc_per_node is the GPU count on this path, not a process count - See .claude/skills/mad-slurm-multinode/references/gotchas.md, section jax_maxtext.
distributed._comment_launcher: Explicit: a missing launcher is read as torchrun. 'docker' selects the basic-environment setup.

_comment: JAX/MaxText Llama-3.1 pretraining, multi-node, against a chosen RCCL build.
gfx950 only. The multi-node cards this drives carry skip_gpu_arch: gfx942, and the fp8
variant is excluded there (the catalog uses nanoo_fp8 on gfx942), so filling this in for
an MI300X-class cluster would launch an unsupported precision path.
Fill every <FILL_...>; archetype-dependent values come from references/cluster-types.md,
including that archetype's own extras (Thor2 QP/RoCE tuning, AINIC RCCL_AINIC_ROCE).
RDMA_CORE_VERSION is Thor2-specific - leave it empty elsewhere, it replaces the image's
RCCL_COMMIT selects the library and RCCL_CMAKE_OPTIONS its build options; <FILL_BUILD_VARIANT>
labels the image so the two travel together. Give each build a unique tag: the tag is the
cache key, so a reused one silently reuses the previous image.
NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 is REQUIRED: madengine's standard SLURM path exports it as 1 by default,
so without this the run silently uses TCP instead of RDMA.

NCCL_DEBUG=INFO with NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,NET so every run records which transport RCCL selected: grep the log for 'via NET/IB/*/GDRDMA'. Restricted to those subsystems it logs at connection setup, not per collective - measured at 0.906-0.909 s/step against 0.936 without it, i.e. no cost to the timing it protects.
